body.statement: For every heavy arm, choose \(J_n\) and the derived \(M_n\) from \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\). Then the deterministic and centered Knight remainders of \(\widehat Q_{a,n,\tau}\) converge uniformly on compact local-parameter sets to \(f_a(\tau)t^2/2\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\theta_a=\vartheta_a\), the preliminary quantiles and every wholly empirical drift component are consistent, and \[\left(\frac{n}{h_{a,n}}\{\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)}{f_a(\tau)}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}.\] By \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\), the endpoint mark step requires only total-variation convergence of the finite score vector \(\Psi_a(Y(a))\) to \(H_a\); no convergence of the full conditional outcome law is required. The true-propensity fixed-quantile law is recovered by replacing the fitted propensity and empirical clip by their population counterparts.
body.justification: It converts the oracle heavy-tail benchmark into a feasible growing-sieve theorem, with its transfer condition proved from primitives.
body.gap: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky prove the observed-true-propensity fixed-quantile law and no feasible propensity-estimation theorem.
body.consumer: Observational QTE analyses can use flexible assignment models while retaining full-population non-Gaussian calibration.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a heavy arm.  Hall inversion gives
\[
t_{a,n}=(c_an)^{-1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\quad
h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\quad
c_an h_{a,n}^{-\gamma_a}\to1.
\tag{27}
\]
The tail-band relative likelihood bound sandwiches fitted tail counts between true counts with multiplicatively perturbed arguments.  At \(t=z/h_{a,n}\), the true expected count is asymptotic to \(h_{a,n}z^{\gamma_a-1}\), and its variance is no larger than its mean.  Uniform Hall inversion and monotonicity thus give
\[
\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1,\qquad
h_{a,n}\widehat p_{a,(\lceil\widehat h_{a,n}\rceil)}\to_P1,\qquad
\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\vartheta_a=\theta_a.
\tag{28}
\]

Put \(z=h_{a,n}\pi_a(X)\) and \(u=\Psi_a(Y(a))\).  Treatment thins the covariate tail by \(z/h_{a,n}\).  Thus iid sampling, (27), Hall regular variation, consistency, unconfoundedness, and \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\) imply, for compactly supported bounded continuous \(g\),
\[
nE_P[\mathbf1(A=a)g\{h_{a,n}\pi_a(X),\Psi_a(Y)\}]
\to\int_0^\infty\!\int g(z,u)H_a(du)(\gamma_a-1)z^{\gamma_a-1}dz.
\tag{29}
\]
Expanding the iid Laplace transform proves marked point-process convergence.  Compensation then gives
\[
S_{a,n}-E_PS_{a,n}\Rightarrow\mathsf Z_{a,\theta},\qquad
S_{a,n}(\tau)=h_{a,n}^{-1}\sum_i
\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}.
\tag{30}
\]
Near zero, the compensated first moment is integrable because \(\gamma_a>1\); at infinity, the second-order bound is proportional to \(z^{\gamma_a-3}\), integrable because \(\gamma_a<2\).

Since \(E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)=E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\), Hall integration gives
\[
E_PS_{a,n}(\tau)\to-\theta_a^{\gamma_a-1}m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}/\gamma_a
=\mu_{a,\theta}(\tau),
\tag{31}
\]
using
\((\gamma-1)\int_0^\theta(z/\theta-1)z^{\gamma-2}dz=-\theta^{\gamma-1}/\gamma\).

Knight's identity,
\[
\rho_\tau(e-v)-\rho_\tau(e)
=-v\psi_{a,\tau}(q_a(\tau)+e)
+\int_0^v\{\mathbf1(e\le s)-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}\,ds,
\tag{32}
\]
with \(v=th_{a,n}/n\), and the conditional density modulus show uniformly on compact \(t\)-sets that the oracle objective is
\[
\frac12f_a(\tau)t^2-t\{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)+\mu_{a,\theta}(\tau)\}+o_P(1).
\tag{33}
\]
The centered curvature variance is \(O(|t|^3h_{a,n}/n)=o(1)\).

For the feasible score, the reciprocal identity and the definition of \(D_{a,n}\) give
\[
\max_\tau|S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}(\tau)-S^{\rm or}_{a,n}(\tau)|
\le CE_{a,n}h_{a,n}^{-1}\sum_i
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\pi_a(X_i)\le M_n/h_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}+\max_\tau|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1).
\tag{34}
\]
Hall integration makes the normalized sum \(O_P(M_n^{\gamma_a-1})\); the two likelihood-lemma conditions make (34) \(o_P(1)\).  Its square-integral bound similarly transfers the curvature.

Positive curvature localizes the smallest convex minimizer, so
\[
\frac n{h_{a,n}}(\widehat q_a-q_a)
\Rightarrow(\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}+\mu_{a,\theta})/f_a.
\tag{35}
\]
We now verify the empirical correction.  At
\(t_{a,k}=F_a^{\pi,-1}(k_n/n)\),
\[
t_{a,k}\asymp(k_n/n)^{1/(\gamma_a-1)},\qquad
nE_P[\mathbf1\{A=a,\pi_a(X)\le t_{a,k}\}]
\asymp k_nt_{a,k}\to\infty.
\tag{36}
\]
The sample-point likelihood bound permits replacement of fitted by true intermediate order statistics.  Integrating the tail empirical survival function shows that the Hill average tends to \((\gamma_a-1)^{-1}\), hence
\(\widehat\gamma_a\to_P\gamma_a\).  Equation (36), the mark modulus, and inner-fold consistency from (35) give
\(\widehat m^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}\to_Pm^{\rm tail}_{a,\tau}\).

For the density estimate, its denominator divided by \(n\) tends to one.  The bounded probability-kernel approximate-identity calculation, the density modulus, and the vanishing clipping-tail mass make the numerator expectation tend to \(f_a(\tau)\).  Its variance is bounded by
\[
\frac C{n\omega_{a,n}}E_P\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,n}\}^2}\right]
=O\!\left(\frac{h_{a,n}^{2-\gamma_a}}{n\omega_{a,n}}\right)=o(1).
\tag{37}
\]
Also \(|\widehat q_a-q_a|/\omega_{a,n}
=O_P\{h_{a,n}/(n\omega_{a,n})\}=o_P(1)\).  Therefore
\(\widehat f_a\to_Pf_a\) and, with (28) and (36),
\(\widehat\mu_{a,\theta}\to_P\mu_{a,\theta}\).  Subtracting the empirical drift in \(\text{def:drift-correction}\) from (35) proves
\[
\left(\frac n{h_{a,n}}\{\widehat q_a^{\rm bc}(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)}{f_a(\tau)}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}.
\]
Using true propensities and the population clip simply removes (34), so it recovers the asserted oracle law.  The mark dependence is only through \(H_a\) by the score-law lemma.
